title: Long-term effects of maternal deprivation on cholinergic system in rat brain.
ehr_evidence: The study used an animal experimental model; male and nulliparous Wistar rats were used, with brain regions collected for AChE activity measurements and morphometric/immunohistochemical analysis (no electronic or computerised health records were analysed).
summary: A controlled experimental animal study examining long-term effects of 24-hour maternal deprivation on postnatal day 9 on acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity and cholinergic (ChAT) fiber density in specific brain structures of male Wistar rats sacrificed at postnatal day 60.
key_findings: AChE activity was significantly decreased in the cortex of MD rats compared to controls (P<0.05).
AChE activity was significantly increased in the hippocampus of MD rats compared to controls (P<0.05).
No change in AChE activity was observed in the thalamus or caudate nuclei.
Density of ChAT-positive fibers was significantly increased in the CA1 region of the hippocampus in MD rats.
Density of ChAT-positive fibers was significantly decreased in the retrosplenial (RS) cortex of MD rats.
No change in ChAT-positive fiber density was noticed in the CA3 region or dentate gyrus (DG).
captured_features: AChE activity (mol/mg) in dorsolateral frontal cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, and caudate nuclei
Density of ChAT-positive fibers (10^3/mm^3) in hippocampal CA1, CA3, dentate gyrus, and retrosplenial cortex
study_design: controlled experimental animal study (maternal deprivation vs. control)
population: male Wistar rats; maternal deprivation on postnatal day 9, sacrificed at postnatal day 60 (2 months)
limitations: Only male animals were used, limiting generalizability across sexes.
Single 24-hour maternal deprivation protocol limits understanding of timing/dose effects.
Limited brain regions examined; additional regions and receptor densities (mAChR, nAChR) not assessed.
